description: Memory-Constrained Data Loading Benchmark - Use cgroups to limit RAM and measure how throughput degrades for LeRobot vs Youmu under memory pressure

userStories.title: Memory-constrained benchmark wrapper script
userStories.description: As a developer, I want a wrapper script that runs the existing benchmark inside a memory-limited cgroup, so that I can measure throughput under realistic memory pressure.
acceptanceCriteria: New script scripts/benchmark_memory_constrained.sh that accepts --memory-limit (e.g. 4G) and passes remaining args to scripts/benchmark_data_loading.py
Uses sudo systemd-run --scope -p MemoryMax=<limit> -p MemorySwapMax=0 to enforce hard memory limit with no swap
Drops page cache before the run via sudo sync && sudo sh -c 'echo 3 > /proc/sys/vm/drop_caches'
Prints the memory limit and confirms cgroup is active before starting
Returns non-zero exit code if systemd-run fails (e.g. insufficient permissions)
Script prints usage when called with --help, exits with error when called without --memory-limit
Tests pass
userStories.notes: System uses cgroup v2 with systemd-run available (cgexec is NOT installed). Use: sudo systemd-run --scope -p MemoryMax=4G -p MemorySwapMax=0 -- python scripts/benchmark_data_loading.py <args>. The --scope flag runs the process in a transient cgroup cleaned up automatically. MemorySwapMax=0 prevents swap fallback so we get OOM kill instead of slow thrashing. Must check sudo access upfront. Python env: . .venv/bin/activate

userStories.title: Full sweep script across RAM limits
userStories.description: As a developer, I want a script that runs the benchmark across all RAM limits and configurations in one command, so that I get a complete dataset unattended.
acceptanceCriteria: New script scripts/benchmark_memory_sweep.sh that iterates over RAM limits [1G, 2G, 4G, 8G, 16G, 32G]
For each RAM limit, drops page cache then runs benchmark_memory_constrained.sh with --backends youmu lerobot and sweep params: num_workers=[0,2,4,8], obs_lens=[1,2,4], batch_sizes=[4,8]
Each RAM limit saves results to benchmarks/memory_constrained/mem_<limit>.csv
If a run is OOM-killed (exit code 137), logs the failure and continues to next configuration
Script prints elapsed time and summary after completion
Uses fewer iterations (50 instead of 200) to keep total runtime reasonable
Tests pass
userStories.notes: Total configs per RAM limit: 2 backends × 4 workers × 3 obs_lens × 2 batch_sizes = 48 configs. Across 6 RAM limits = 288 total configs. With 50 iterations each this should be manageable. OOM kill returns exit code 137 (128 + SIGKILL=9). The script should run each backend separately within each RAM limit so that a youmu OOM doesn't skip the lerobot run.

userStories.title: Aggregate results and write report
userStories.description: As a developer, I want a Python script that aggregates per-RAM-limit CSVs into a single report showing how throughput changes with memory pressure for each backend.
acceptanceCriteria: New script scripts/analyze_memory_benchmark.py that reads all CSVs from benchmarks/memory_constrained/
Produces combined CSV benchmarks/memory_constrained/combined_results.csv with a memory_limit column

Generates markdown report benchmarks/memory_constrained_benchmark_report.md with: summary table of best throughput per backend per RAM limit, full results table, analysis of crossover point, OOM failure notes
Unit tests for CSV aggregation and report generation logic
Tests pass
userStories.notes: Read the memory limit from the filename (mem_1G.csv -> 1G). The summary table should show for each RAM limit: youmu samples/sec (best config), lerobot samples/sec (best config), ratio. Highlight the crossover point where youmu >= lerobot. Note which RAM limits had OOM failures and for which backend.

userStories.title: Run the full memory-constrained benchmark
userStories.description: As a developer, I want to run the full sweep and produce the final report so that we have concrete data on memory pressure impact.
acceptanceCriteria: Run scripts/benchmark_memory_sweep.sh to completion (all 6 RAM limits)
Report at benchmarks/memory_constrained_benchmark_report.md contains results for at least 4 of 6 RAM limits
Report clearly shows whether Youmu throughput advantage increases under memory pressure
Combined CSV has data from all successful runs
userStories.notes: Run in tmux to avoid interruption: tmux new-session -d -s bench './scripts/benchmark_memory_sweep.sh'. At 1G limit, both backends may OOM — that's expected and fine. The interesting data points are 2G-16G where LeRobot should degrade while Youmu stays stable.
